questions.question: What does the `auto` keyword in `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 800px` add?
options: It makes the section always 800px tall
It lets the browser remember the section's last rendered size and use that instead of the 800px estimate once it has been rendered
It disables content-visibility in unsupported browsers
It automatically calculates the size before rendering
questions.explanation: 800px is only the initial placeholder. After the section renders, the remembered real size is used, which reduces scrollbar jumps and layout shift.

questions.question: How does content skipped by `content-visibility: auto` differ from content hidden with `display: none`?
options: Skipped content is removed from the DOM
Skipped content is still painted but invisible
Skipped content stays in the DOM and accessibility tree and can still be found with find-in-page
questions.explanation: content-visibility: auto only skips rendering work for offscreen content; it remains accessible and searchable, and find-in-page reveals it.

questions.question: Why is this loop slow? `for (const row of rows) { row.style.width = container.offsetWidth / 2 + "px"; }`
options: Each iteration writes a style and then reads offsetWidth, forcing a synchronous layout every time
String concatenation with px is expensive
style.width cannot be set from JavaScript
questions.explanation: The write invalidates layout and the next read forces it to be recalculated immediately. Reading once before the loop avoids this layout thrashing.

questions.question: A developer adds `* { will-change: transform; }` to speed up animations. What is the likely result?
options: All animations become free on every device
The rule is ignored because will-change only works on :root
Many compositor layers are created, using lots of GPU memory and possibly making low-end devices slower
questions.explanation: Each promoted layer costs memory. will-change should be applied to a few elements just before they animate, not globally.
